sections.title: Bulk macro ranges — not a weight-based equation
lines: Around 200 lbs: protein 340–400 g, carbohydrates 450–600 g, fats 90–120 g daily.
At 150 lbs: protein 220–300 g, carbohydrates 350–500 g, fats 75–100 g daily.
The PDF calls these ballpark numbers to adjust to the individual. It does not define an interpolation equation.
PDF p.8: 6–8 meals per day. The meal-plan heading on PDF p.15 instead says 6–7 meals, or every 2–3 hours. Both are retained.
Increase calorie intake gradually week by week while monitoring body-fat changes. No fixed weekly calorie increment is specified.

sections.title: Cheat meals
lines: Start with 1–2 cheat meals per week; the source says to adjust according to metabolism.
Source timing: post-workout, especially on a lagging body-part day.
The listed examples include Persian food, In-N-Out or Habit burger (3×1 animal style with fries and diet coke), sushi or Korean BBQ.

sections.title: Supplement protocol · source reference only
lines: Upon waking, with 16 oz water: 2 scoops Carnigen, 1 scoop AMINOJECT, 1/2 scoop LIPOCIDE IR, 1 scoop ISOJECT (Evogen Nutrition).
Mid-morning: 1 scoop CELL KEM, 1 scoop GLYCOJECT.
Pre-workout, 10 minutes before training: 2 scoops EVP PLUS, 1 scoop Carnigen, 1 scoop Glycoject.
Intra-workout: sip 1.5 scoops Cell Kem and 2 scoops Glycoject throughout workout.
Post-workout, 30 minutes after workout: 2 scoops IsoJect, 2 scoops Glycoject, 1 scoop AMINOJECT.
Before bed: 1 scoop Cell Kem.

These are the supplied book’s product-specific quantities, retained for reference. Product formulations and scoop sizes are not specified. The app does not convert them to ingredient dosages or schedule supplement intake.

cardio.title: Bulk cardio protocol
lines: Start with 20 minutes steady-state cardio, low–moderate intensity. The source prefers morning stair climber or treadmill.
Source hydration: 16 oz water before morning cardio.
If weight/body fat climbs too rapidly: increase cardio by 5 minutes and decrease calorie intake until weight stabilizes.
If weight/body fat drops too quickly: decrease cardio by 5 minutes and increase calorie intake until weight stabilizes.
No frequency per week or exact calorie adjustment is specified.

sections.title: Exact initial base-diet calculation
lines: Protein (g/day) = body weight in lbs × 1.4.
Carbohydrates (g/day) = body weight in lbs × 1.4.
Fat (g/day) = body weight in lbs × 0.25.
Calories: protein 4 kcal/g, carbohydrates 4 kcal/g, fat 9 kcal/g.
The source also states a protein range of 3.0–3.8 g/kg. This is separate from the initial-base equation; it is not substituted for that equation.
The printed example table rounds fats. At 125 lbs, the equation gives 31.25 g fat but the source example prints 32 g. Both are shown without silently reconciling them.

sections.title: Establish the baseline
lines: Source definition: a base diet maintains body weight. Follow the set macros for 5 days, then analyze weight change.
If losing weight, the source adds 25 g carbohydrate per day until fluctuations stop; if gaining, it removes 25 g per day until fluctuations stop. Protein and fat stay consistent.
The source example 220 g protein / 250 g carbohydrate / 50 g fat is an example, not the equation for all users.

sections.title: Adjusted diet and re-feed rules
lines: Start the adjusted diet by reducing base-diet carbohydrate by 25–50 g/day (approximately 8–16 g carbohydrate removed from 3 of 6 meals).
The source tracks morning scale weight. It describes a re-feed after a 3–4 lb loss, usually 5–7 days, doubling carbohydrate in every meal.
Re-feed examples also change foods and include a post-workout meal; their fat and carbohydrate totals do not always equal the simple doubling rule. The examples are preserved separately.
The source describes an expected 1–2 lb increase after re-feed. These are author statements, not outcomes the app guarantees.
No automated dieting or rapid-loss rule changes your targets. Review and explicitly apply a chosen calculation.

sections.title: Meal frequency and source portion examples
lines: 5–7 meals per day, every 2.5–3 hours.
Source examples: 4 oz chicken = 28 g protein; 1 oz sweet potato = 6 g carbohydrate; 1 c brown rice = 45 g carbohydrate; 2 tbsp peanut butter = 17 g fat.
These are the book’s stated examples, not a verified food-composition database. Food diary entries continue to require your portion and source.

sections.title: Source inconsistencies retained
lines: The monthly example starts with baseline 220 g protein / 240 g carbs / 38 g fat; that differs from both the introductory example and a direct formula calculation at 160 lbs.
Day 27 lists 155 g carbs, but day 28 returns to 180 g with no explanation. The values are preserved exactly.
The day-16 re-feed example is 400 g carbs; the doubling rule applied to 180 g would give 360 g. Neither is silently changed.

Intra-workout: sip 1 scoop Cell Kem.

lines: Fasted cardio 4× per week: 40 minutes on stair climber, steady state, minimum 80–100 steps per minute.
Fasted sprints 2× per week: 20 × 50-yard sprints; walk back 50 yards as rest, then repeat.

cardio.title: Weeks 5–6
lines: Fasted cardio 5× per week: 40 minutes on stair climber, steady state, minimum 80–100 steps per minute.
Fasted sprints 1× per week: 20 × 50-yard sprints; walk back 50 yards as rest, then repeat.

cardio.title: Weeks 7–8
lines: Fasted cardio 5× per week: 30 minutes on stair climber, steady state, minimum 80–100 steps per minute.
Fasted sprints 1× per week: 20 × 50-yard sprints; walk back 50 yards as rest, then repeat.
Post-workout cardio 5× per week: 30 minutes stair climber, steady state, minimum 80–100 steps per minute.
